claims.text: When an http or https URL writes no port, the default port is 80 for http and 443 for https.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 §4.2.1 http URI Scheme and §4.2.2 https URI Scheme

claims.text: A client must turn the host name of a URL into an IP address before it can open a connection, usually by asking DNS, because a connection is opened to an address and not to a name. The name localhost always means the machine you are on, address 127.0.0.1.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 §4.3.3 (resolving the host identifier before connecting); RFC 1034 §2.1; RFC 6761 §6.3 (localhost)

claims.text: In this lab both ports are reached over TCP: the client opens a TCP connection to the address and port before it sends the request (port 8080 speaks HTTP/1.1). The lab passes the host's ports 8080 and 8443 to its own, where Caddy listens, so localhost:8080 reaches the same Caddy from either side.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9112 §9.1 Establishment; RFC 9110 §4.3.3; docker-compose.yml ports and network_mode service:lab at stage-0

claims.text: For an https URL the TLS handshake runs after the TCP connection is established and completes before the HTTP request is sent.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9112 §9.7 (ClientHello, then first request after the handshake); RFC 9110 §4.3.3

claims.text: One HTTP request names one target, so every further file a page needs costs its own request and its own response; a page opened once therefore shows several rows in the network tab.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 §7.1 Determining the Target Resource; §3.1 Resources

claims.text: The first line of an HTTP/1.1 response is the status line, which states how the request went before anything else is read; when the server could not fulfil the request, the response says so.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9112 §4 Status Line

claims.text: A page's HTML is a text file of tags that names the files the page needs; a browser fetches embedded ones (img, link, script) on its own but follows a hyperlink only on activation; a script is a program run inside the page and can send more requests.
claims.source_hint: HTML Living Standard, 'Embedded content' and 'Links: following hyperlinks / navigation'

claims.text: A TCP connection attempt to a port with nothing listening is refused, while an attempt whose bytes get no answer times out; the two are different failures.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9293 §3.10.7.3 (RST on connection to closed port); connect(2) ECONNREFUSED vs ETIMEDOUT

claims.text: The server presents a certificate as its proof of identity during the TLS handshake, and a certificate the client does not trust aborts the exchange after the TCP connection is open and before any HTTP request is sent.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 §4.3.4 https Certificate Verification; RFC 8446 §4.4.2 Certificate, §6.2 Error Alerts

claims.text: At stage-0 donhang.local resolves on the host machine only after 127.0.0.1 donhang.local is added to the hosts file, usually checked before DNS; the lab lists it in its own hosts file. HTTPS is on port 8443, plain HTTP on 8080.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/STAGE.md and Caddyfile at tag stage-0; hosts(5) / name service switch resolution order; docker-compose.yml extra_hosts at stage-0

claims.text: scripts/http/trace-request.sh at stage-0 re-runs itself inside the lab box, where lab is a resolvable name, and prints address 172.28.0.12 for lab, a connection on port 8080, Protocol : TLSv1.3, a first line HTTP/1.1 200 OK, and three 200 lines in step 5.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/scripts/http/trace-request.sh and outputs/stage-0/scripts/http/trace-request.txt (CI capture)

claims.text: In the script, curl -D - writes the response's header block to standard output, -o /dev/null discards the body, and -w with %{http_code} %{url_effective} prints the status code and the URL asked for, one line per exchange.
claims.source_hint: curl manual page: --dump-header (-D), --output (-o), --write-out (-w); confirmed by the CI capture of this script

claims.text: www/index.html at stage-0 contains three anchor links (/login.html, /cached.html, /redirect) and no img, link or script element.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/www/index.html at tag stage-0

claims.text: Because that page embeds nothing, the HTML asks the browser for no further file; login.html and cached.html load only if the reader clicks them. An extra row the browser adds on its own, such as the site icon, does not come from this HTML.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/www/index.html at stage-0 combined with HTML Living Standard hyperlink activation

claims.text: When a page fails and the browser shows an error, the category of that error (name, connection, certificate, server) usually points at the step of the chain to investigate first, even though browsers word the message differently.
claims.source_hint: author's recommendation; condition: the browser reports an error rather than a slow page

claims.text: An http or https URL is written as the scheme, then ://, then an authority holding a host name and an optional port, then a path; the path is the part after the host.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 §4.2.1 (http-URI = "http" "://" authority path-abempty) and §4.2.2

claims.text: The name lookup, the TCP connection and the TLS handshake all finish before the server starts producing the requested page, because the request that names the page is sent only after them.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 §4.3.3 (resolve, connect, secure, then send the request); RFC 9112 §9.7

claims.text: A status code of 200 on the response's first line means the request succeeded.

Each command after step 1 resolves its own name and opens its own connection. set -euo pipefail (a line not shown) stops the script at a step that cannot complete (no address, connection or encryption); step 2 (nc && echo) leaves an empty block and goes on; a 503 response does not stop it.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/scripts/http/trace-request.sh at stage-0; openssl-s_client(1) and curl(1) connection handling

claims.text: In the script, grep -A1 also prints the line after each match, nc -z -w 3 only tests the connection and gives up after 3 seconds, and piping echo into openssl s_client gives it an empty input so it closes right after the handshake.
claims.source_hint: grep(1) -A; nc(1) -z, -w; openssl-s_client(1) (closes on end of input); CI capture of trace-request.sh

claims.text: A browser's developer tools include a network panel that lists the exchanges a page makes, one row each, with how long each took; opening it before reloading makes the page's rows appear.
claims.source_hint: browser developer tools documentation (no docs root in content/versions.yaml; see open_questions)
